source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect all monitoring records related to air quality and industrial emissions, including data from air quality sensors, CEMS (Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems), and stack tests. Pay close attention to any recorded violations of emissions standards and any notable trends over time.

3. Identify the pollutants of interest.
Determine which pollutants are being monitored and should be included in the report. Common industrial pollutants include particulate matter (PM), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and hazardous air pollutants (HAPs).

4. Rate emissions against regulatory standards.
Compare the emissions data with the relevant local, regional, and national regulatory standards. Document any instances where the emissions exceed these standards.

5. Analyze data trends.
Use appropriate statistical methods to analyze the data, identifying trends over time and any peaks or anomalies that might indicate excessive emissions events.

6. Document emission events and violations.
